question: What is the main goal of managing childhood illnesses in primary health care?
explanation: Primary health care focuses on stopping common, preventable conditions from becoming fatal through early detection and standard treatment. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T5#BMP126_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why do health workers look at the whole child instead of treating just one symptom?

options.A: National health policy prohibits treating single complaints in primary clinics
options.B: Children frequently suffer from multiple overlapping conditions at the same time
options.C: Hospital administrative forms require documenting every single body system
options.D: Single symptoms never provide enough data to write a valid prescription

explanation: Sick children often present with co-existing illnesses like malaria and pneumonia simultaneously, requiring a broad assessment approach. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T5#BMP126_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which international organizations jointly developed the IMCI strategy in the 1990s?

options.A: Doctors Without Borders and Red Cross

explanation: The World Health Organization and UNICEF created IMCI to tackle the leading killers of young children in developing nations. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T5#BMP126_U1_T5_h2)

question: What was the main limitation of traditional disease-specific training that IMCI was designed to fix?

options.A: It treated illnesses in isolation instead of addressing overlapping symptoms
options.B: It was too expensive for local primary health centers to implement
options.C: It focused entirely on nutrition while ignoring infectious diseases
options.D: It required doctors to be present for every basic consultation

explanation: Old training methods looked at single diseases, which did not fit reality when a child had both fever and cough together. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T5#BMP126_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three main pillars of the IMCI strategy?

options.B: Promoting healthy family and community practices
options.D: Improving health worker case management skills

explanation: Surgical training is not part of IMCI; the strategy focuses on clinical case management, health systems, and community practices. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T5#BMP126_U1_T5_h3)

question: A clinic has well-trained staff, but all malaria medications are out of stock. Which IMCI pillar is failing here?
explanation: Drug supply chain management and facility readiness fall directly under the health systems strengthening pillar of IMCI. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T5#BMP126_U1_T5_h3)

question: What does a general danger sign in an under-five child tell the health worker?

options.A: The child only needs routine immunization updates
options.B: The child has a severe condition requiring urgent attention
options.C: Laboratory tests are required before any action is taken
options.D: The mother should take the child home to rest for two days

explanation: General danger signs point to severe illness that demands immediate medical intervention and possible emergency referral. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T5#BMP126_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why is the inability to drink or breastfeed classified as a critical danger sign?

options.A: It proves the child has a permanent neurological deficit in the brain
options.B: It only occurs when a mother has stopped producing breast milk entirely
options.C: It indicates the child has a blocked nasal passage from a common cold
options.D: It rapidly leads to severe dehydration and prevents oral medication administration

explanation: When a child cannot drink, they cannot take oral rehydration salts, syrups, or water, making dehydration and deterioration happen very fast. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T5#BMP126_U1_T5_h4)

question: What action is required under IMCI guidelines when a child's condition is classified in the Pink category?

options.B: Routine follow-up visit after one week
options.D: Urgent pre-referral treatment and hospital transfer

explanation: The pink row represents a severe classification, demanding emergency pre-referral treatment and transfer to a higher facility. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T5#BMP126_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why does IMCI use symptom-based color-coded charts instead of waiting for lab test results?

options.A: To replace the need for physical examination by trained health workers
options.B: To prove that laboratory testing is entirely unnecessary in clinics
options.C: To reduce the paperwork required for clinic record books
options.D: To enable rapid life-saving treatment decisions in resource-limited settings

explanation: Many primary clinics lack functional labs, so IMCI uses physical signs to guide urgent action immediately. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T5#BMP126_U1_T5_h5)

question: When should a health worker give the very first dose of a prescribed oral treatment for a sick child?

options.A: Right there in the health facility
options.B: Only if the child refuses to take syrup
options.C: At the follow-up visit three days later
options.D: After the child arrives back home

explanation: Giving the first dose at the clinic allows the health worker to check that the child can swallow it and show the caretaker how to do it. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T5#BMP126_U1_T5_h6)

question: Why is it important to advise mothers to continue breastfeeding and feeding a sick child?

options.A: Stomach acid destroys all disease-causing parasites during digestion
options.B: Nutritional intake supports immune function and prevents rapid weight loss
options.C: Eating prevents the child from crying while taking bitter syrups
options.D: Food acts as a direct chemical antidote against bacterial infections

explanation: Sick children burn extra energy fighting infection; withholding food worsens malnutrition and delays recovery. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T5#BMP126_U1_T5_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of Community-Based IMCI (C-IMCI)?

options.A: Training mothers to perform surgical procedures at home
options.B: Eliminating the need for facility-based health workers
options.C: Replacing primary health centers with mobile surgical vans
options.D: Extending life-saving child health interventions directly into villages and homes

explanation: C-IMCI takes health education and basic care out of the clinic and into the community where families live. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T5#BMP126_U1_T5_h7)

question: How do community-based volunteers support the success of the IMCI strategy?

options.A: By helping families recognize danger signs early and seek prompt care
options.B: By conducting laboratory blood transfusions in village squares
options.C: By writing medical prescriptions for severe malaria cases
options.D: By inspecting primary health center financial records

explanation: Early recognition at the community level prevents delays in seeking care, which is a major cause of preventable child deaths. [learn more](BMP126_U1_T5#BMP126_U1_T5_h7)
